USER TURN 9
but agent b can stop at any reason.  thi sis diffrent.  send is diffretne form notifciaiotn remember we3 talekd aout messages vs system notficaiotns?

ASSISTANT TURN 9 (1 messages, last privileged)
[earlier] You’re right. I conflated execution notifications with agent replies. ```text Agent-authored message B decides what to communicate B → message send → A “I checked X. Here are my findings.” System notification Service observes an execution event Service → notification → subscribed CLI / SDK “Turn T ended.” “Run R timed out; stopping is unconfirmed.” ``` B stopping does not mean it finished the task, produced a reply, or wants A awakened. ```text Agent B Codex Our service CLI / SDK │ │ │ │ │ Turn ends │ │ │ ├───────────────►│ │ │ │ │ Execution event │ │ │ ├───────────────────►│ │ │ │ │ System notification│ │ │ ├───────────────────►│ │ │ │ │ │ │ No automatic message to A ``` A timed wake-up is different again: it delivers message content that someone explicitly arranged earlier. I need to correct the design: observing B’s execution ending must not automatically become an agent-authored message or a claim of task completion. Any “wake A when this event happens” behavior needs an explicit subscription or rule, with the event’s system origin preserved.

USER TURN 10
we might get double messages so heres an idea.  if b stops, and there was no message from b, we could send system ntoficaiont to original?

ASSISTANT TURN 10 (1 messages, last privileged)
[earlier] Yes—a fallback system notification could avoid the usual duplicate. ```text Agent A Service Agent B │ │ │ │ Request work │ │ ├──────────────────►├───────────────────►│ │ │ │ │ │ B sends an explicit reply │◄──────────────────┼────────────────────┤ │ │ Records reply │ │ │ │ │ │ B stops │ │ │◄───────────────────┤ │ │ Reply exists │ │ │ → no fallback │ ``` If B stops without replying: ```text Agent A Service Agent B │ │ │ │ │ B stops │ │ │◄───────────────────┤ │ │ No related reply │ │◄──────────────────┤ │ │ System notification: │ │ “B's execution ended without a reply. │ │ Task completion is unconfirmed.” │ ``` The important detail is “related reply.” An unrelated message from B shouldn’t suppress this notification. We need a request ID carried by B’s reply. For a reply racing with B stopping, the service should check its durable reply record before creating the fallback. A reply that arrives after the fallback was already delivered can still produce two communications; we shouldn’t promise to eliminate that case entirely. One distinction remains: should this fallback appear only in A’s subscribed CLI/SDK events, or also be delivered into A’s model context as an explicitly system-origin notification? The latter lets A notice and respond while idle.

ASSISTANT TURN 11 (2 messages, last privileged)
[earlier] I’ll check PR1’s actual notification contracts and client code. I’ll also record your scope decision: explicit B→A messages for now; automatic completion callbacks and fallback notifications are deferred.
[earlier] PR1 did include notifications. I checked the code, including the merged commit. My explanation blurred their meaning. ```text PR1 notifications → client software ├── endpoint/changed │ Service/endpoint changes, with ordering and scope checks ├── Native Codex observation │ App-server events through an attached observation connection └── ACP session updates Conversation updates through the ACP client PR1 agent messages → recipient model input └── Explicit message send from B to A ``` Evidence: [endpoint notification contract](/Users/shravansunder/Documents/dev/project-dev/codex-router.feat-agent-messaging-v2/crates/communication-protocol/src/endpoint_inventory.rs:17), [SDK notification receiver](/Users/shravansunder/Documents/dev/project-dev/codex-router.feat-agent-messaging-v2/crates/communication-client/src/control_connection.rs:367), and [native observation client](/Users/shravansunder/Documents/dev/project-dev/codex-router.feat-agent-messaging-v2/crates/communication-client/src/observation_session.rs:88). PR1 does not provide a system-notification inbox that automatically wakes another model, or the “B stopped without replying” fallback. I’ve updated the design to use C now: B explicitly sends its reply. Automatic completion callbacks and fallback notifications are deferred. Scheduling still tracks execution state, but that tracking does not manufacture an agent reply.

USER TURN 12
so when is it skuppseod to be used?

ASSISTANT TURN 12 (1 messages, last privileged)
[earlier] Notifications are for software watching what happens. Messages are for giving an agent information to act on. ```text Codex / Host CLI or SDK client Human / UI │ │ │ │ “Turn ended” │ │ ├──────────────────────►│ Update displayed status │ │ ├────────────────────────►│ │ │ │ │ “Endpoint offline” │ Show disconnected state │ ├──────────────────────►├────────────────────────►│ ``` Use PR1 notifications when: ▸ Agent Studio needs to update status or display streamed output. ▸ A CLI observer needs to show activity. ▸ Client software needs to notice endpoint changes and reconcile state. They do not automatically enter another agent’s conversation. ```text Agent B → message send → Agent A Reads and acts on the message ``` For your current workflow, B uses `message send` to communicate with A. The service uses native observations to track scheduled execution, while `wake send` arranges future model input. Three different jobs: observe, communicate, and arrange delivery.
